name: Hu
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.
catalog_citation: Svantesson, Jan-Olof. 1991. Hu - a language with unorthodox tonogenesis. In J.H.C.S. Davidson (ed.), Austroasiatic Languages: Essays in honour of H. L. Shorto, 67-79. London: SOAS. (SEAlang SALA archive PDF)
catalog_locator: p.67 (introduction), p.69 (Minor syllables), p.71 (Tones and vowels)
catalog_quote: p.67: From a general phonological point of view, the most interesting phenomenon is the development of a two-tone system where the tones are not the reflexes of voiced/voiceless proto-initials, as is most often the case in Mon-Khmer two-tone (or two-register) languages. Instead, the tones are the reflexes of the long/short vowel opposition which existed in Proto-Palaungic (inherited from Proto-Mon-Khmer). ... p.69: Minor syllables. As in other Northern Mon-Khmer languages, most non-compound words are monosyllabic or sesquisyllabic, i.e. consisting of a major syllable preceded by an unstressed minor syllable (cf. Shorto 1960). Minor syllables have a syllabic sonorant (such as m in θmphúp 'lung') or a (probably) non-contrasting vowel which I have written as a (kaʔà 'two'). ... p.71: Tones and vowels. audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all three deciding passages (pp.67, 69, 71) are verbatim at the stated pages in the SEAlang scan we hold of Svantesson 1991 (read as page scan; no text). (2) Deciding source: a 1991 phonology article by Svantesson from a small one-speaker vocabulary; primary and competent, but not the fullest description - Glottolog lists a 226-pp 2016 reference grammar in Mandarin (Jiang & Shi, Kunge = Hu) and a 2004 Minzu Yuwen sketch (Li Jinfang), and Wikipedia cites Sidwell 2015 pp.49-50 for a syllable template with stress on the major syllable and presyllables 'always unstressed', which agrees with our classification. (3) No open copy of any of these could be downloaded: for the session was exhausted, DuckDuckGo/Semantic Scholar/WorldCat downloads were refused (connection refused / 429), Bing returned irrelevant results; the three works still to obtain are print-only or CNKI.
